requirements.fact: Road rash requires prompt irrigation with clean water and covered sterile dressing to prevent infection.
requirements.misconception: Minor road rash heals faster when left open to the outdoor air without cleaning.
pamphlet_excerpts: Roadway Hazards: Surface potholes and slick sewer grates cause loss of steering control.
Hydration Planning: Riders must consume water and electrolyte fluids before feeling extreme thirst.
Concussion Assessment: Suspected head injury victims must stop riding and seek medical evaluation.
Wound Management: Clean road abrasions thoroughly with potable water before applying sterile gauze.
requirements.pamphlet_summary: Cyclists prevent common roadway injuries by scanning road surfaces for debris and maintaining safe following distances. First aid preparation requires carrying sterile dressings and oral electrolytes to manage trauma and dehydration.
requirements.safety_callout: Never move a downed rider suspected of cervical spine trauma unless immediate environmental danger threatens life.
socratic_questions: How do changing weather conditions alter your stopping distance on wet pavement?
What immediate symptoms distinguish heat exhaustion from life-threatening heatstroke on a ride?
Why must you replace a bicycle helmet after a single high-impact collision?
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Route Hazard Assessment: Identify surface obstacles and narrow road shoulders prior to group departures.
Step 2 - Medical Kit Packing: Pack sterile dressings, adhesive bandages, and electrolyte powders in saddlebags.
Step 3 - Heat Stress Response: Move overheated cyclists into shade and loosen tight helmets or jerseys.
Step 4 - Incident Documentation Reporting: Record trail accident details and notify adult leadership of all injuries.

sub_requirements.fact: Cyclists must hold their line or scan behind before maneuvering around pavement obstacles.
sub_requirements.misconception: Swerving suddenly around road debris without looking backward is the safest avoidance tactic.
sub_requirements.pamphlet_summary: Cyclists manage risks by maintaining scanning vigilance twenty seconds ahead to spot gravel, animals, and car doors. Group formations require verbal callouts for road hazards to protect trailing riders.

sub_requirements.fact: Heat cramps require sodium replacement through balanced electrolyte beverages alongside gentle muscle stretching.
sub_requirements.misconception: Scouts experiencing muscle cramps only need plain tap water to recover full strength.
sub_requirements.pamphlet_summary: Trailside first aid treats lacerations, friction blisters, and environmental temperature extremes during remote rides. Responders stabilize sprains with splints and monitor concussed riders for cognitive confusion.

requirements.fact: Riding against traffic violates vehicle codes and increases collision risk at intersections fivefold.
requirements.misconception: Cyclists should ride facing oncoming vehicle traffic so they can see approaching cars.
pamphlet_excerpts: Vehicle Status: Bicycles hold statutory vehicle rights and must obey all traffic signals.
Lane Positioning: Ride on the right side except when turning left or passing.
Signal Communication: Extend your left arm straight horizontally to indicate an impending left turn.
Door Zone Hazards: Maintain four feet of clearance from parked cars to avoid opening doors.
requirements.pamphlet_summary: State vehicle codes grant bicycles the rights and responsibilities of motor vehicles on public roadways. Cyclists must ride with traffic flow and execute lane changes using progressive rearward visual shoulder checks.
requirements.safety_callout: Never filter forward along the right side of large trucks waiting at red traffic signals.
socratic_questions: Under what roadway conditions does state law permit a bicyclist to take the full travel lane?
Why are sidewalk cyclists particularly vulnerable to collisions at driveways and intersections?
How do hand signals change a motorist's behavior when approaching a bicycle from behind?
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Traffic Law Review: Check municipal codes regarding sidewalk bans and mandatory bicycle lane rules.
Step 2 - Shoulder Check Scan: Look over your left shoulder to confirm motor vehicle clearance before moving.
Step 3 - Hand Signal Execution: Display the hand signal clearly for three seconds prior to initiating turns.
Step 4 - Intersection Lane Control: Take the center of the travel lane when lanes are too narrow.

requirements.fact: An improperly fastened helmet can slip off the forehead completely during an initial impact.
requirements.misconception: A loose helmet strap provides sufficient protection as long as the hard shell covers the skull.
pamphlet_excerpts: Helmet Certification: Bicycle helmets must display a CPSC safety standard approval sticker inside.
Level Fitment: Position the front helmet rim two finger widths above the brow.
High Visibility Clothing: Fluorescent neon jerseys increase rider contrast against complex urban background environments.
Eye Protection: Clear or tinted shatterproof lenses shield eyes from grit and insects.
requirements.pamphlet_summary: Proper cycling safety requires an approved helmet meeting Consumer Product Safety Commission standards fitted snug and level. High-visibility apparel and padded cycling shorts prevent road glare accidents and saddle chafing on extended tours.
requirements.safety_callout: Discard and replace any bicycle helmet that has sustained an impact or shows hairline shell cracks.
socratic_questions: How do the Scouting America Bike Safety Guidelines dictate night riding lighting requirements?
Why are dark cotton t-shirts dangerous choices for rural highway cycling trips?
What physiological problems can occur when riding without padded cycling gloves on rough roads?
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Helmet Placement Level: Position the helmet flat on your head without tilting backward or forward.
Step 2 - Side Strap Adjustment: Form a snug V shape directly beneath each earlobe with side sliders.
Step 3 - Chin Buckle Tension: Fasten the chinstrap allowing only one finger between strap and throat.
Step 4 - Gear Securing Protocol: Tuck loose shoelaces into shoes and secure wide pant cuffs with bands.

requirements.fact: Household sprays dissolve factory grease and attract abrasive grit that ruins bicycle chain pins.
requirements.misconception: Motor oil or household penetrating sprays work effectively to lubricate bicycle drive chains.
pamphlet_excerpts: Tire Pressure: Check sidewall markings to inflate tires to their recommended pressure range.
Brake Pad Clearance: Ensure brake pads strike the wheel rim without touching the tire rubber.
Chain Lubrication: Apply bicycle lubricant to chain rollers and wipe away excess surface oil.
Quick Release Security: Close quick release levers so they curve inward and leave palm impressions.
requirements.pamphlet_summary: Routine bicycle maintenance uses the ABC Quick Check protocol to ensure air pressure, brake pads, and chains function safely. Proper adjustments of seat height and handlebar reach prevent chronic joint strain and ensure responsive control.
requirements.safety_callout: Never raise a seatpost or handlebar stem past the etched minimum insertion safety line.
socratic_questions: What mechanical hazards occur when riding on bicycle tires inflated below recommended minimum pressure?
How do you detect worn brake cables before they snap under emergency stopping pressure?
Why must quick release cam levers be clamped closed rather than spun tight like wingnuts?
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Tire Air Inspection: Inflate inner tubes using a floor gauge pump to specified sidewall PSI.
Step 2 - Brake Squeeze Check: Squeeze brake levers to verify one thumb width clearance before bar contact.
Step 3 - Drivetrain Cleaning Lube: Degrease chain links thoroughly before applying specialized synthetic bicycle lubricant drops.
Step 4 - Cockpit Bolt Tightening: Tighten stem and seatpost binder bolts evenly to prevent unexpected slippage.

sub_requirements.fact: Tire pressure must be measured with a dedicated pressure gauge against the sidewall specifications.
sub_requirements.misconception: Tire firmness can be accurately gauged simply by pressing your thumb into the tread.
sub_requirements.pamphlet_summary: A systematic pre-ride inspection examines wheel true, headset tightness, quick-release clamps, and cable tension. Catching loose hardware before riding prevents catastrophic mechanical failure at road speed.

sub_requirements.fact: A properly fitted saddle requires the rider to dismount or stand on tiptoes when stopped.
sub_requirements.misconception: A rider should be able to sit flat-footed on the ground while remaining seated on the saddle.
sub_requirements.pamphlet_summary: Set saddle height so the cyclist maintains a slight five to fifteen degree knee bend at bottom stroke. Handlebars should allow comfortable elbow flex without causing excessive spinal curvature or wrist pressure.

sub_requirements.fact: Limit screws physically restrict cage travel, while cable tension controls indexing alignment between cogs.
sub_requirements.misconception: Derailleur limit screws control the indexing cable tension between gear shifts.
sub_requirements.pamphlet_summary: Adjust brake barrel adjusters to remove cable slack and center the pads squarely on the rim braking track. Set derailleur high and low limit screws so the chain cannot overshoot into the spokes or frame.

sub_requirements.fact: Cassette teeth do not require lubrication, as excess oil collects grit that accelerates tooth wear.
sub_requirements.misconception: Thick automotive grease should be sprayed across the entire surface of the gear cassette.
sub_requirements.pamphlet_summary: Apply targeted bicycle lubricant to chain pivot pins, derailleur pulleys, and brake pivot points while avoiding wheel rims. Wiping off exterior fluid keeps road grime from forming grinding paste inside moving parts.

sub_requirements.fact: Metal tools pinch inner tubes and scratch rim beds, causing immediate puncture flats.
sub_requirements.misconception: Metal screwdrivers work well as substitutes for plastic tire levers when prying off stubborn beads.
sub_requirements.pamphlet_summary: Repairing a flat tire involves unseating the bead with tire levers, patching or replacing the inner tube, and inspecting the tire casing. Checking the inside casing removes sharp thorns or wire fragments before reinstallation.

sub_requirements.fact: State laws mandate a white headlight visible from five hundred feet regardless of clothing color.
sub_requirements.misconception: Wearing light-colored clothing eliminates the legal mandate for active bicycle headlights after dusk.
sub_requirements.pamphlet_summary: Local ordinances require bicycles ridden after sunset to feature a white front headlight and red rear reflector or lamp. Many jurisdictions also mandate audible warning devices like bells and functional braking systems.

requirements.fact: Grabbing only the front brake can throw the rider forward over the bicycle handlebars.
requirements.misconception: Slamming only the front brake lever is the quickest way to stop safely in emergencies.
pamphlet_excerpts: Power Pedal Start: Position your dominant pedal at the two o'clock position to begin forward motion.
Threshold Emergency Braking: Shift rider body weight backward over the rear wheel during hard braking stops.
Straight Line Scanning: Practice looking over your left shoulder while keeping handlebars tracking perfectly straight.
Predictable Turning Arc: Lean bicycle gently into turns while keeping inside pedal raised at twelve.
requirements.pamphlet_summary: Mastering bicycle handling involves smooth power starts, straight-line balance, predictable cornering, and rapid emergency braking. Cyclists must execute shoulder scans and standard hand signals without deviating from their travel line.
requirements.safety_callout: Always shift body weight backward behind the saddle when executing sudden emergency stops.
socratic_questions: Why must you keep your inside pedal raised at the top position when cornering tightly?
How does shifting to an easier gear before coming to a stop improve your next startup?
What happens to your steering line when you turn your head to scan backward?
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - High Pedal Launch: Set the lead pedal to two o'clock and push down smoothly.
Step 2 - Straight Tracking Balance: Maintain steady cadence while keeping the front wheel centered within the lane.
Step 3 - Shoulder Scanning Drill: Glance backward over your shoulder without pulling the handlebar in that direction.
Step 4 - Controlled Emergency Stop: Slide weight behind saddle while squeezing both brake levers with controlled modulation.

requirements.fact: Riding ahead breaks the buddy system and leaves trailing riders stranded during roadside emergencies.
requirements.misconception: Toughing it out alone ahead of the group shows cycling endurance and leadership.
pamphlet_excerpts: Buddy System Discipline: Ride within conversational distance and monitor your partner for fatigue or mechanicals.
Touring Pace Cadence: Spin steady pedal cadence between seventy and ninety revolutions each minute continuously.
Trail Etiquette Rules: Yield the trail to hikers and announce passes to avoid startling horses.
Rest Stop Nutrition: Consume carbohydrate snacks and fluids every forty-five minutes during long distance rides.
requirements.pamphlet_summary: Completing either the road biking or trail biking option requires rigorous route planning and strict adherence to the buddy system. Riders maintain continuous visual contact, monitor fatigue levels, and coordinate pacing across all scheduled touring miles.
requirements.safety_callout: Never ride two abreast on narrow winding roads with blind curves or heavy vehicle traffic.
socratic_questions: How do you adjust your group pacing when a buddy experiences sudden dehydration or fatigue?
What specific factors determine whether you choose the road option versus the trail option?
Why is drafting closely behind another cyclist dangerous during troop group rides?
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Route Elevation Mapping: Chart the course profile, resupply points, and emergency bailout locations in advance.
Step 2 - Pre-Ride Buddy Briefing: Review hand signals, planned pace, and rest stop locations with your partner.
Step 3 - Cadence Nutrition Management: Maintain steady pedaling and take regular fluid sips during each ride segment.
Step 4 - Post-Ride Log Entry: Record total mileage, elapsed time, weather conditions, and terrain in your cycling logbook.

sub_requirements.fact: The fifty-mile tour requires progressive physical conditioning through mandated shorter rides to prevent severe exhaustion.
sub_requirements.misconception: Scouts can skip intermediate training rides and successfully complete the fifty-mile tour on enthusiasm.
sub_requirements.pamphlet_summary: The road biking option focuses on highway navigation, road safety tests, and multiple progressive endurance tours culminating in a fifty-mile ride. Cyclists must navigate traffic safely and sustain pedaling rhythm over asphalt terrain.

sub_requirements.fact: Skidding causes loss of braking traction and damages trail tread surfaces, violating trail conservation ethics.
sub_requirements.misconception: Skidding rear wheels around tight dirt corners is an effective mountain bike steering technique.
sub_requirements.pamphlet_summary: The trail option tests off-road bike handling over gravel, roots, rocks, and uneven dirt paths across multiple off-road treks. Cyclists adapt tire pressures for traction and navigate varying trail grades while respecting wilderness path ethics.
